job.descriptionText:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

You will run the external audit calendar for our SOX 404 program as we scale toward an IPO. That means coordinating with our external auditors across the year, aligning testing windows with control owners, educating our control owners, and keeping requests and deliverables on schedule. You will also own SOX scoping and risk assessment cycles, deficiency tracking, and status reporting, and help roll out our GRC platform so the program runs from one system of record instead of spreadsheets. You will scale the program through AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual effort and speed up our SOX program.

This role reports to the Head of Business Controls and works closely with everyone on the SOX and Internal Audit team. This is an individual contributor role for someone who keeps a complex program on schedule, writes clearly, and makes the program simpler each cycle.

Key responsibilities

- Own the annual SOX audit calendar, including interim and year-end testing windows, walkthrough schedules, and key deliverable dates agreed with external auditors.
- Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for external auditor requests. Triage, route, and track each request to closure, including PBC (provided-by-client) lists and evidence deliveries.
- Coordinate auditor walkthroughs and fieldwork with process owners, control owners, and the SOX Testing team, so each control owner is asked for the same evidence once.
- Track auditor findings, management responses, and deficiency follow-ups, and report status to Internal Audit leadership.
- Prepare control owners and process owners for auditor sessions, and get evidence delivered on time without direct authority over them.
- Lead the annual SOX scoping and risk assessment, including quarterly refreshes, and support the annual Fraud Risk Assessment, so the program has appropriate scope and coverage under COSO.
- Monitor BP and IT SOX testing and report status to leadership and share status with external auditors
- Lead work with the business to improve control documentation, including education of templates and SOX guidance.
- Find optimization and automation opportunities across the SOX lifecycle through the use of AI.
- Support the rollout of the GRC tool for SOX, including control libraries, workflows, evidence requests, and testing templates.
- Define the data and reporting requirements the platform must meet, and test that it produces what the program needs.
- Run the quarterly sub-certification process and report results to leadership
- Own SOX program status reporting: dashboards and metrics for leadership, audit calendar progress, and deficiency and remediation status.
- Own status reporting for the full SOX lifecycle: scoping and risk assessment, testing, deficiencies and remediation, segregation of duties (SOD), SOC 1 report reviews, the fraud risk assessment, and audit calendar progress.

Minimum qualifications

- Big 4 audit firm experience on SOX 404 or ICFR engagements, including managing audit calendars, PBC requests, and fieldwork with external audit teams.
- Experience working directly with external auditor teams on requests, testing schedules, and findings, from the company side.
- Several years of hands-on SOX 404 experience, including scoping, risk assessment, control documentation, testing, and deficiency evaluation.
- Working knowledge of the COSO framework, ICFR, and PCAOB standards.
- Experience developing or maintaining Risk and Control Matrices and process documentation or flowcharts.
- Experience implementing or administering a GRC systems
- Experience reporting program status, metrics, and issues to senior leadership.
- Ability to get control owners to deliver on time without authority over them.
- Clear writing and calm coordination under deadline pressure.
- A Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience.

Preferred qualifications

- In-house SOX experience at a pre-IPO or newly public company.
- Experience running a fraud risk assessment.
- CPA, CISA, or similar certification.
- Comfort with SQL or data tools for reporting, and experience building lightweight automations, including with Claude.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

About the Role

Email is one of our most important storytelling channels at Superpower, and we want a designer who owns it. You’ll design the emails our members get at every stage: lifecycle flows, onboarding, results notifications, product launches, newsletters and promotional campaigns. Your job is to make every send look sharp, read clearly and get people to take action.

You’ll work closely with our design and content teams. Content brings the words and the strategy, design sets the brand standard, and you turn both into emails that perform. When the team needs extra hands on a marketing campaign or a product moment, you’ll pitch in. Email is your home base, but nobody here is boxed into one channel.

We call this “founder mode” for design. You’re in the weeds, you ship, and you go looking for the places that need help most.

What You'll Do

- Own email design end to end, from lifecycle and automated flows to campaigns, newsletters and transactional emails

- Partner with the content team on structure, hierarchy and how copy and visuals work together in the inbox

- Work with the design team to keep email aligned with the brand system, and help extend that system with email components and templates

- Build modular, reusable templates that let the team ship faster without losing quality

- Design for how email actually renders: mobile first, dark mode, and the quirks of different email clients

- Use performance data (open rates, click-through, conversion) to shape your designs, and run tests to find what works

- Ship fast. Action produces information, so your first version doesn’t need to be perfect. It needs to exist.

- Give and receive direct feedback. Radical candor is how we raise the bar together.

- 3–6+ years of design experience across brand, digital, product, or a combination, with a strong focus on digital

- A portfolio that shows range: product screens, campaign work, web design, and a few pieces outside digital marketing

- Strong fundamentals in typography, layout, color, hierarchy, and interaction design

- An understanding of how email renders across clients and devices

- Comfort with ambiguity and context-switching — you can reprioritize quickly without losing quality

- Speed and craft. You don’t treat them as opposites.

- Proficiency in Figma. Familiarity with prototyping, basic motion, or front-end code is a bonus

- Self-directed and proactive. You ask "how would I act if this were my company?" and then do it

- Genuine care about health, wellness, or human performance

Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Datasets Team

Wayve’s Datasets team own the driving data that our AI Driver learns from, covering ingestion, annotation (automatic and manual), retrieval and data quality. Our data is growing from hundreds of petabytes towards exabyte scale, and not all of it is equally valuable for training. This team decides what we keep and where, and builds the systems that make those decisions work in practice.

🧠 Your day-to-day

- Implement and iterate filtering, retention and offload policies across hot, cold, archive and delete storage

- Build the data movement and pipelines that our pre-ingestion selection model depends on

- Decide where and how selection models run, balancing compute cost against data value

- Build early, low-compute decision points that avoid expensive standardisation and enrichment of low-value data

- Work with the storage and data infra teams, and monitor data quality to make sure our datasets reflect what model training needs

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

- Turning our dataset strategy into working systems: moving, filtering, retaining and offloading driving data at hundreds of petabytes

- The engineering behind our pre-ingestion selection mode(s)l: how data moves, where the model runs and how offload policies work

- Delivering large, measurable storage-cost savings through early, low-compute decisions

- Making sure our datasets contain the most useful behavioural and environmental coverage for training. This is as much a data quality challenge as a software engineering one

- Working as a pair with our dataset strategy lead (who design and builds the models) and closely with the data infra team, shipping practical solutions quickly

👤 You should apply if:

- You’re a senior data or software engineer who has run data ingestion or data quality pipelines at petabyte scale

- You’re strong in Python and Spark, with cloud data engineering experience

- You have good judgement on data filtering and quality, and know how to check you haven’t discarded valuable data

- You ship practical solutions quickly and are comfortable iterating on live systems

- You’re a software engineer at heart, building the systems around models rather than the models themselves

- You enjoy working closely with data infra and storage teams

- You bring experience in AV, robotics, fleet data or high-volume IoT, or with retention, offload and data lifecycle policies (a bonus rather than a requirement)

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚗 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻 — Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

📋 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

- Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

- Intro with the hiring manager (Find out more about the role, your exp etc; 1 hour)

- Competency Interviews (System design and technical leadership; 2 hours)

- Deep Dive (Domain Interview; 1 hour)

- Final interview: mission & values alignment (1 hour)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependent):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partner discounts and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

The best outcome is a case that never gets opened because the product problem behind it was found and fixed. Everything in the support experience is in scope. You decide where to start.
- You'll define the end-to-end experience Claude delivers: diagnosing a billing failure, resolving it or escalating it, recognizing when the same failure is showing up across many customers, filing the bug with repro steps and a proposed fix, getting that to the engineering team that owns the driver, following up with the customer to confirm the issue was actually resolved, and confirming the category actually goes away once the fix ships.

Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our MEGA Team

Multi-Embodiment Generalist Agent (MEGA) team within Wayve Labs as a founding member.

MEGA is building foundation models for general-purpose robots beyond self-driving vehicles. Our focus is on creating intelligent agents that can perceive, reason, move and manipulate the physical world across diverse embodiments, including mobile manipulators, dual-arm platforms and humanoids.

🧠 Your day-to-day

- You enjoy working hands-on with real robots and are comfortable debugging across hardware, software, and ML systems.

- You can move between research exploration and pragmatic engineering execution.

- You have strong judgement around experiment design, data quality, and model evaluation.

- You communicate clearly across research, engineering, and product teams.

- You are excited by 0→1 ownership and ambiguity in a fast-moving research environment.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

Leading the development of an offline 3D reconstruction capability that builds high-quality 3D world geometry from vehicle sensor data in dynamic scenes. The system will draw on localization and mapping, state estimation, and sensor fusion to produce offline 3D geometric reconstructions and best-estimate ego motion from heterogeneous vehicle platforms and sensor suites. The work will support internal validation, data enrichment, and model development by turning raw sensor data into reliable, quality-assessed 3D ground-truth outputs.

🙌 You should apply if you have:

- Experience in robot manipulation; working with robot hardware.

- Experience with C++ and Python in robotics or ML environments.

- Strong robotics and machine learning fundamentals, with the ability to translate research into robust systems.

- Publications in top-tier conferences such as ICRA, CoRL, or IROS are highly valued.

- PhD preferred; MS acceptable with strong relevant experience.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

- Initial call / recruiter screen: general background, current situation, interests and Wayve company information & hiring context.

- Competency Interviews: programming and code review.

- Deep-dive technical interviews: domain knowledge & system design.

- Final interview: mission & values alignment.

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Every dollar Anthropic earns and every dollar it spends on compute has to reach the books correctly, and the volume grows with Claude usage. That data comes from across the company and from partners: usage and billing, compute, infrastructure assets, leases. Products and pricing models keep launching, and each one adds another path into the books. Our goal is a continuous close with zero material issues, with audit-grade controls.

You’ll build the platform that gets us there: one front door for every finance event, an append-only ledger, and an accounting engine that posts each event exactly once. This is a distributed systems problem with an unusually high correctness bar. The system has to be right to the cent, replay cleanly and explain any number as of any date, at that volume. You will shape its architecture. Its users include Claude agents, which read and write through the same APIs and controls as people.

You’ll work closely with SWEs in Billing, Compute and Infra on shared contracts and APIs, and with product owners, finance operations and internal audit to turn accounting and controls requirements into designs. You don’t need a finance background. If you have built backend systems where correctness matters, we will teach you the domain.

Responsibilities

- Design and build the front door into finance and its governed contracts: APIs for apps and agents, an event bus for systems that publish, adapters for vendor apps and reports, data-quality gates, and processing that posts every event exactly once, with replay and backfill
- Drive the build of the accounting ledger and engine: an append-only ledger with idempotent posting, a rules framework that turns business events into journal entries, translation into the ERP, and period locks
- Design and build the SDKs and frameworks that finance apps and agents build on
- Build controls into the platform as code: immutable audit trail, maker-checker, scoped access and segregation of duties
- Build and run the production services that other engineering teams call in real time, such as the tax and collections services in the billing flow, and own their reliability: uptime, latency, throughput and correctness targets agreed with those teams
- Shape the platform’s technical direction: architecture, engineering standards and design reviews

- Experience designing and running high-volume, event-driven systems (publish/subscribe, streaming) with idempotent processing, replay and backfill
- Experience designing relational data models and writing SQL for complex, versioned data
